key_insight: Optimization theory better explains practical machine learning when it preserves algorithmic features such as sketching, clipping, normalization, and approximate orthogonalization.
engineering_relevance: Training reliability depends on matching objectives, clipping schedules, and learning rates to the actual update rules and numerical approximations.
method: Analyze submodel objectives to distinguish biased Independent Subnetwork Training from unbiased Model-Agnostic Sparsified Training.
Study quantile clipping schedules and combine smoothed normalization with error compensation for distributed private optimization.
Develop layer-wise generalized smoothness and the Gluon framework for Muon- and Scion-style methods.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports convergence guarantees, near-optimal nonconvex rates under heavy-tailed noise, and validation of a layer-wise smoothness model, but gives no datasets or numerical results.
watch_item: In Muon, less precise approximate orthogonalization requires smaller stepsizes, so precision and learning rate should be tuned together.
paper_title: Understanding Practical Optimization in Machine Learning
